audit_phase: Phase 9C — State Transition and Physiological Deterioration Timing
scientific_conclusion: Physiology-guided state trajectories demonstrate significant incremental temporal association with subsequent acidemia beyond current state (progression vs reversal OR > 2.3x, p < 0.001), although biological compensation boundaries constrain global discrimination at >=30 minutes to AUROC ~ 0.569. Hybrid alerting achieves 94.74% specificity and 0.075 false alerts/hour with 15.0-minute median lead time.

decision_matrix.details: Horizon filters verified; 505/547 patient rank invariance explains identical >=60m and >=45m AUROC (0.5360).
Progressing trajectories exhibit 2.3x-2.6x higher patient-level acidemia risk vs reversing trajectories (p < 0.001).
Exact 547/547 patient maximum state (S_max) reconstruction confirmed.
All 5 state thresholds derived a priori in Phase 9B with zero test-fold leakage.
19/19 clinical descriptors documented with physiological FIGO rationale and zero leakage.
Synthetic future perturbation confirmed max |Delta X| = 0.000000000000 across all variables.
T_state < T_delivery verified for all windows; trajectory classified using historical data only.
Lead times verified (State 1: 27.5m, State 2: 17.5m, State 3: 12.5m, State 4: 7.5m).
Policy parameters (tau=0.28, 0.85*tau, S>=2, P>=2) anchored to training baseline distribution.
Hybrid Policy 5 reproduces 31.82% sens, 94.74% spec, 0.075 FAR/hr, 15.0m lead time.
AUROC tables reproduced bit-for-bit across all 5 models and 6 horizons.
B=2,000 paired patient bootstrap CIs and p-values quantified for all models.
Trajectory adds meaningful stratification within matched states and improves near-delivery discrimination.
Severe acidemia (pH <= 7.05, N=41) exhibits consistent 21.3x jump across states (1.23% to 26.19%).
Full audit suite executes cleanly and deterministically from raw dataset to final outputs.
